mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically across the four weekly snapshots from -46.0 to -40.6. This momentum reflects progressive reopening and will persist into the next 28 days, raising the next four-week mean above the last four-week mean.
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS fell from 49.0 to 27.3 in the latest week, a drop exceeding 15 points. This signals a shift from outdoor leisure toward indoor activities, including shopping, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as people substitute park visits with retail trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: After a week-on-week PARKS decline greater than 15 points, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved from -55.6 to -53.7 while WORKPLACES remains near -46.0. This joint pattern indicates that non-commute trips are returning even though office commuting is suppressed, driving higher retail and recreation footfall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises while WORKPLACES remains below -40
failure_condition: When TRANSIT rises while WORKPLACES is below -40, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated at -20.4 while RETAIL_REC is much lower at -40.6. This gap reflects a temporary reallocation of spending to groceries; as grocery demand normalizes, spending shifts back to retail, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: Under GROCERY_PHARM > -25 and RETAIL_REC < -40, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has declined from 15.1 to 13.0, meaning fewer people are staying home. This behavioral shift increases out-of-home retail footfall and will lift RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as the stay-at-home component continues to erode.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM worsened from -19.4 to -20.4 in the latest week, indicating renewed precautionary shopping. This signals reduced general mobility and will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next week as households retrench toward essential trips only.
failure_condition: After GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20.0, the next 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not lower than its prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp PARKS decline combined with TRANSIT stabilisation signals that outdoor leisure demand is shifting into indoor retail settings. The joint movement predicts higher RETAIL_REC over the next week as consumers redirect trips from parks to shops.
candidate_trigger: PARKS down >10 points and TRANSIT up >1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: When PARKS falls more than 10 points and TRANSIT rises more than 1 point week-on-week, the next 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady reopening regime with WORKPLACES flat between -48 and -44, retail recovery is driven by leisure and shopping rather than commuting. Continued policy easing without new restrictions will raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays between -48 and -44, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 28-day mean.
